title: NPPAD Zero-Shot LLM Explorer
task: Frozen LLMs, no fine-tuning and no examples, classify one 60-second window of 12 NPPAD sensor channels (6 samples per channel, given as numbers in a text prompt) into one of 12 accident classes. 48 held-out windows per protocol, strict scoring: anything but exactly one class code counts as wrong.

protocols.t0_20: Early (t0 = 20 s, the Task E placement)

methods.name: Claude — v1 plain prompt
methods.takeaway: The best of the plain prompts — and still far below the trained models.

methods.name: Claude — v2 context prompt
methods.takeaway: Adding long explanations hurt: on early windows its answers collapsed onto a couple of classes.

methods.name: Claude — v3 chain-of-thought
methods.takeaway: Best onset accuracy of the prompt arms, but macro F1 fell — no clean win for reasoning prompts.

methods.name: Claude — v4 tree-of-thoughts
methods.takeaway: No gain over the plain prompt at either protocol.

methods.name: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (local)
methods.takeaway: Answered the same single class for every window at both protocols — exactly chance level.

methods.name: Gemini 3 Flash (gemini-3-flash-preview)
methods.statusNote: Partial run: 57 of 96 windows answered before the free-tier quota stopped the run. The t0=100 protocol is complete (48/48); only 9 of 48 t0=20 windows were answered, so no t0=20 score is claimed.
methods.takeaway: Partial run. Its completed onset score sits below Claude’s plain prompt; the early protocol was never finished.

methods.name: ChatGPT (gpt-5.2)
methods.statusNote: Not run: the key authenticates, but the OpenAI account has no API credits remaining. Every chat completion call returned HTTP 429 (no credits), so no ChatGPT answers could be collected.
methods.takeaway: Not run — the API account had no credits, so no answers exist and no number is estimated.

methods.name: FETA-style DTW few-shot (3 exemplars)
methods.takeaway: The one genuine LLM-side gain: retrieved labeled examples nearly doubled onset accuracy. Still far below the trained models, and it fails on early windows.

methods.name: ReasonTSC-style plug-in
methods.takeaway: Perfect at onset only because the LLM repeated the trained model’s top answer on all 48 windows. The LLM added nothing in either direction.

methods.name: ReasonTSC — full replication
methods.takeaway: The paper’s correction claim did not reproduce: across 96 windows the reasoning rounds made 0 corrections and 1 breakage — one decision changed, for the worse.

methods.name: Health-LLM-style statistical summary
methods.takeaway: A small onset accuracy bump over the plain prompt but slightly lower F1, and it collapsed on early windows.

methods.name: LLMTime-style serialization
methods.takeaway: The worst arm, near chance at both protocols: its per-window rescaling deletes the absolute magnitudes that carry the signal in this data.

methods.name: MOMENT-1 frozen-embedding probe
methods.takeaway: A trained logistic probe on frozen time-series embeddings — level with FETA at onset. Strong, but it is a trained probe, not a zero-shot LLM result.

methods.name: Random few-shot control (3 exemplars)
methods.statusNote: Original run NOT trustworthy: two blinded agents returned answers matching the true labels on all 12 suspect windows (P100_W37–W48), consistent with reading the label file instead of classifying blind. Values shown are the corrected closed-protocol clean re-run.
methods.takeaway: Shown only as the corrected clean re-run. The original headline score must not be cited.

sensitivity.label: Original run, excluding the 12 suspect windows (n=36), t0=100

methods.name: Plot-image zero-shot (12-panel plots)
methods.statusNote: Original run NOT trustworthy: the same label-leak anomaly on the suspect windows, and its t0=20 answers duplicated the statistics arm’s answers on 48 of 48 windows. Values shown are the corrected closed-protocol clean re-run.
methods.takeaway: Shown only as the corrected clean re-run. The original headline score must not be cited.

sensitivity.label: Original run, excluding the 12 suspect windows (n=36), t0=100

trainedReference.name: Trained MultiRocket+HYDRA (reference)
trainedReference.scope: full test split (n=240 at t0=100, n=244 at t0=20), reference
trainedReference.takeaway: The trained reference on the full test split. Every LLM method is compared against this bar — and at t0=20 even the trained models are weak, because the plant has barely responded inside the window.

verdict: Plain zero-shot prompting on NPPAD behaves exactly as the published literature predicts: near chance on a 12-class multivariate task, and prompt engineering alone does not fix it. Retrieval of similar labeled examples (FETA) is a real prompt-level improvement and roughly doubled onset accuracy, but stays far below trained models and fails on early windows. Plugging a trained model into the prompt only "reaches" trained-model performance because the LLM defers to it completely.
